title: Object Literals and Property Access Check
description: Create objects and read/update properties with dot and bracket notation.

questions.explanation: `age` was updated to 37. Missing keys like `city` return `undefined`, not an error.

questions.prompt: Given `const key = "name"` and `const user = { name: "Ada" }`, what is the difference between `user.key` and `user[key]`?
questions.explanation: Dot notation looks for a property literally named `key`. Bracket notation uses the value of the variable (`"name"`).

questions.prompt: When is bracket notation **required** (dot notation cannot work)?

options.text: When the key comes from a variable or is not a valid identifier

questions.explanation: Dot needs a fixed identifier. Dynamic keys and keys with spaces/punctuation need brackets.

options.text: No — `const` only blocks reassigning the variable `user`
Yes — property writes throw in all modes
Only if the property was created with `let`

questions.explanation: `const` freezes the binding, not the object. You can still update properties unless you use `Object.freeze`.

questions.prompt: What does reading a missing property return?
questions.explanation: Missing own keys evaluate to `undefined`; they do not throw.
